expectations.text: test.txt content was read and incorporated
expectations.evidence: The output file notes/test-notes.md contains the repo file listing (AGENTS.md, build.py, coding, os-config, etc.) which matches what test.txt would contain. The content was read and incorporated into the note.

expectations.text: File saved to a categorized directory (not repo root)
expectations.evidence: File saved at notes/test-notes.md, inside a 'notes/' categorized directory, not the repo root.

expectations.text: Content has been polished or structured for clarity
expectations.evidence: The raw file listing was wrapped in a code block for readability, given a descriptive title 'Test Notes — Repository File Listing', and placed in a structured markdown document with frontmatter. The content is organized and clear.

expectations.text: YAML frontmatter contains title, tags, created, and summary fields
expectations.evidence: Frontmatter contains: title: 'Test Notes — Repository File Listing', tags: [test, notes, repo-structure], created: 2026-04-05, summary: 'A test note containing a snapshot listing of files and directories in the km repository root'. Also includes 'related' field.

Both exist in outputs. MANIFEST.md has Content Map including 'notes/' and Recent Additions entry for the new file. Root README.md lists 'notes/' directory. notes/README.md links to test-notes.md with description.

claims.claim: A new 'notes/' directory was created for miscellaneous content
claims.evidence: The notes/ directory exists in outputs with README.md and test-notes.md inside it.

claims.claim: Root README.md was updated to include the new notes/ directory
claims.evidence: Root README.md contains '- [notes/](notes/) — Miscellaneous notes, scratch content, and quick captures'.

suggestions.assertion: Content has been polished or structured for clarity
suggestions.reason: This assertion is subjective and would pass for minimal formatting changes (e.g., just wrapping in a code block). Consider checking for specific structural improvements like headings, descriptions, or meaningful organization beyond what the raw input had.

suggestions.assertion: test.txt content was read and incorporated
suggestions.reason: Since the eval runs in an isolated outputs directory, there is no actual test.txt to read. This assertion checks whether the executor simulated reading it. Consider providing a real test.txt fixture with known content and asserting that specific lines appear in the output.

eval_feedback.overall: Assertions cover the key outcomes. The 'content polished' assertion could be more specific, and using a real fixture file would make the content-incorporation check more rigorous.
